He subsequently settled in England, where he became a prominent polo team patron and competitive player.

long_biography.plain_text:
Former Bank of Moscow president Andrey Borodin trained in international finance in Russia and Germany. After attending a specialist physics and mathematics school, he studied at the Moscow Finance Institute and spent an academic year at the University of Passau. Dresdner Bank then provided practical experience in Dortmund and Frankfurt, including work in its financial institutions department.

Polo has become a sustained competitive commitment for Borodin through his Park Place team. The side reached the Queen’s Cup final during its first season of high-goal polo in 2018. He also played alongside Jason Wates, Juan Britos and Hilario Ulloa in the Park Place line-up that won the U.S. Open in 2023.

uncertainties.detail: Investor is the strongest alternative after the bank disposal, but neither active portfolio management nor a principal present asset has been positively established. The direct 2014 interview is too old to prove current inactivity. Current polo ownership supplies a sporting identity, not proven dominance in private wealth. Passive owner would be an inference from silence; operator is historical. A less-specific supported current relationship is therefore unavailable.

Broad self-made follows direct Forbes attribution and documented operating/equity wealth. It does not imply a blank-slate start. Municipal establishment of the bank and Borodin’s advisory role are acknowledged; family support or inheritance is not established and no narrower subtype is asserted.

The personal website biography and Forbes profile are historical. Their role lists and Moscow residence are not carried into present-tense fields. Established UK base is consistent with later sporting coverage. No current net-worth estimate is proposed.
